change: Case dropped
why: Dropped (third time). No credible source documents harm that actually happened to people or nature near Medupi after the 2010 IBRD loan. The death and asthma figures are modelled estimates. Residents' accounts come from a Fair Finance Coalition report whose authors say they did not test any causal link to Medupi (Daily Maverick, 2023). The 2017 Sunday Times report on Marapong centres on the older Matimba plant. The 2023 SAHRC action was a probe of a complaint, not a finding. Eskom's own Marapong monitoring (May 2024) recorded no exceedances of national air limits. The Inspection Panel found no current harm in 2011. Police dispersal of striking construction workers (2015) and a shooting of two workers by an unknown gunman were labour incidents not caused by the plant or forces acting for it. Complaint link ip:65 dropped with it.

change: Case dropped
why: Dropped: Bank role and timing do not match the harm. The harms in the Panel's 2007 report (a logging company cutting Batwa medicinal and caterpillar trees and destroying fields and sacred sites; villages and fields inside concessions without compensation; entry fees; promised schools and clinics missing) were caused by concession holders, most with titles from before the Bank's 2003 and 2005 operations. The Bank did not finance or require logging: its forest conditions were extending the 2002 moratorium on new concessions and starting a legal review meant to cancel illegal titles. The Panel said only that the review 'may have inadvertently' encouraged swaps and faster logging, on 'anecdotal information', and that the Batwa claims 'could not be properly assessed'. Its compliance findings were about procedure (no environmental assessment, Pygmies not identified). No source documents harm from the concessions the review later confirmed (2009). Complaint link ip:37 dropped with it.
